Home  Health  Aide                      Event  Category:  Health  Professions
………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
 
Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary  /  Collegiate  
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  1  competitor  Round  Two:  Skill(s)  assessment   
New  for  2026-2027
 Editorial  updates  have  been  made.     
Event  Summary
 Home  Health  Aide  allows  members  to  gain  the  knowledge  and  skills  required  for  supporting  patients  in  their  homes.  This  
competitive
 
event
 
consists
 
of
 
two
 
rounds.
 
Round
 
one
 
is
 
a
 
written,
 
multiple-choice
 
test,
 
and
 
the
 
top-scoring
 
competitors
 
will
 
advance
 
to
 
Round
 
Two
 
for
 
the
 
skills
 
assessment.
 
This
 
event
 
aims
 
to
 
inspire
 
members
 
to
 
be
 
proactive
 
future
 
health
 
professionals
 
and
 
equip
 
them
 
to
 
serve
 
patients
 
in
 
a
 
home
 
health setting.   
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.   ●  Round  One:  Proper  business  attire,  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform,  or  attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area.    ●  Round  Two:  Attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area. 
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  Photo  ID for  both  rounds  ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  eraser  for  the  test.  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (Rd1-optional)  ●  Manual  watch  with  second  hand  required  for  Round  2  for  Vital  Signs  (no  iWatches)  ●  Tape  ½“  or  1”  ●  Bandage  Scissors  ●  Gloves  non-latex  (3  pairs  per  competitor)  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
Ofﬁcial  References   The  references  below  are  used  in  the  development  of  the  test  questions  and  skill  rating  sheets:  a.  Balduzzi,  Suzann.  Homemaker  Home  Health  Aide .  Cengage  Learning.  Latest  edition. b.  Leahy,  Fuzy,  &  Grafe.   Providing  Home  Care:   A  Textbook  for  Home  Health  Aides.   Hartman  Publishing,  Inc.   Latest  edition.  
ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  All  competitors  will  receive  a  test  and  answer  sheet.   The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple-choice  items  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here. 
Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.   All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
 Home  Health  Aide   ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  1  of  14  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

Written  Test  Plan  The  written  test  for  Home  Health  Aide  is:  ●  Responsibilities  and  Legal/Ethical  Issues  -  10%  ●  Effective  Communication  -  6%  ●  Infection  Control  and  Safety  -  10%  ●  Body  Systems  and  Common  Disorders  -  40%  ●  Caring  for  Special  Populations  -  24%  ●  Basic  Healthcare  Skills  -  10%  
Sample  Test  Questions  Sample  Round  One  Test  Questions  1.  A  dying  client  tells  the  home  health  aide  "Please  leave  me  alone,  I  just  want  to  be  by  myself.”  What  stage  of  grief  is  the  client  experiencing?  (Balduzzi  pp  355)  A.  Acceptance  B.  Anger  C.  Bargaining  D.  Depression  2.  What  is  the  general  term  that  refers  to  a  serious  loss  of  mental  abilities  such  as               thinking,  remembering,  reasoning,  and  communicating?  (Fuzy  pp  156)  A.  Alzheimer’s  disease  B.  Dementia  C.  Vascular  stroke  D.  Parkinson’s  disease    3.  A  nebulizer  would  most  likely  be  ordered  to  treat  a  client  with  which  condition?             (Balduzzi  p  329)  A.  Iron  deﬁciency  anemia  B.  Arteriosclerosis  C.  Emphysema  D.  Congestive  heart  failure   
ROUND  TWO-  Skills  Assessment
 
1.  The  top  competitors  from  Round  One  will  advance  to  Round  Two.  The  number  of  advancing  competitors  will  be  determined  by  the  scores  obtained  in  Round  One  and  the  space  and  time  available  for  Round  Two.  Round  Two  ﬁnalists  will  be  announced  on-site  at  ILC  per  the  conference  agenda.  
2.  Round  Two  is  a  selected  skill(s)  assessment.  The  Round  Two  skills  approved  for  this  event  are:  Skill  I:  Taking  an  Adult  Tympanic  Temperature  3  minutes  
Skill  II:  Taking  an  Apical  Pulse  3  minutes  
Skill  III:  Emptying  a  Urinary  Drainage  Unit  4  minutes  
Skill  IV:  Changing  a  Dry  Dressing  Using  Non-Sterile  Technique  5  minutes  
Skill  V:  Measuring  and  Recording  Intake  and  Output  5  minutes  
Skill  VI:  Caring  for  Dentures  5  minutes  
Skill  VII:  Moving  a  Patient  Up  in  Bed  Using  a  Drawsheet  3  minutes  
Skill  VIII:  Applying  Elasticized  Stockings  (One  leg)  5  minutes  3.  For  all  skills,  body  ﬂuids  will  be  a  simulated  product.  
 Home  Health  Aide   ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  2  of  14  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   
4.  The  selected  skill(s)  will  be  presented  to  competitors  as  a  written  scenario  at  the  beginning  of  the  round.  The  scenario  will  be  the  same  for  each  competitor.  A  sample  scenario  can  be  found here. Some  scenarios  may  involve  the  combination  of  multiple  skills.  If  the  event  rating  sheets  are  combined,  it  is  not  necessary  to  repeat  a  task  a  second  time.  An  example  would  be  competitors  would  not  need  to  identify  the  patient  twice.  
5.  Timing  will  begin  when  the  scenario  is  presented  to  the  competitors  and  will  be  stopped  at  the  end  of  the  time  allowed.  The  scenario  is  a  secret  topic.  Competitors  MAY  NOT  discuss  or  reveal  the  secret  topic  until  after  the  event  has  concluded  or  will  face  penalties  per  t he  GRR s. 
6.  Competitors  must  complete  all  skill  steps  listed  in  the  guidelines,  even  if  the  steps  must  be  simulated/verbalized.  (If  the  equipment  is  available,  the  competitors  would  complete  all  skill  steps  as  the  scenario  warrants.  The  competitors  will  simulate/verbalize  the  steps  if  the  equipment  is  unavailable.)  
7.  Judges  will  provide  information  to  competitors  as  directed  by  the  rating  sheets.  Competitors  may  ask  questions  of  the  judges  while  performing  skills,  if  the  questions  relate  to  the  patient's  condition  and  will  be  included  in  the  scenario  or  judge  script.  
8.  Competitors  must  use  all  equipment  correctly  and  safely.  Judges  will  stop  a  student  and  not  award  points  for  a  step  if  they  see  a  competitor  is  about  to  cause  a  risk  of  harm  or  about  to  damage  equipment  or  other  supplies.   
Final  Scoring 
 1.  The  competitor  must  earn  a  score  of  70%  or  higher  on  the  combined  skill(s)  in  Round  Two-Skills  Assessment   in  order  
to
 
be
 
recognized
 
as
 
an
 
award
 
winner
 
at
 
the
 
ILC.
 
  2.  The  ﬁnal  rank  is  determined  by  adding  the  round  one  test  score  plus  the  round  two  skill  score.  In  the  event  of  a  tie,  
the
 
highest
 
test
 
score
 
will
 
be
 
used
 
to
 
determine
 
the
 
ﬁnal
 
placement.
  
Future  Opportunities
 The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!   The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.
 
As
 
a
 
HOSA
 
member,
 
you
 
are
 
eligible
 
to
 
become
 
a
 
HOSA
 
Lifetime
 
Alumni
 
Member-
 
a
 
free
 
and
 
valuable
 
opportunity
 
to
 remain  connected,  give  back,  and  help  to  shape  the  future  of  the  organization.  Learn  more  and  sign  up  at hosa.org/alumni.

Home  Health  Aide   Skill  I:  Taking  an  Adult  Tympanic  Temperature
 
Time:  3  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________ Division:  ________ SS  ________ PS/C    Judge’s  Signature: _________________________
 
 Skill  I:  Taking  an  Adult  Tympanic  Temperature   Possible  Awarded      1.    Gathered  equipment:   tympanic  thermometer,  disposable  probe  cover,  daily  record  sheet,  and   gloves.  
1  0  
  
    2.    Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene  and  put  on  gloves.  
2  0  
  
3.    Explained  skill  to  patient.  
2  0  
  
4.   Placed  new  probe  cover  on  thermometer.  
1  0  
  
5.   Turned  thermometer  on.  
1  0  
  
6.   Pulled  top  of  ear  up  and  back.  
1  0  
  
7.   Pressed  top  button  as  inserted  covered  probe  in  ear.  
1  0  
  
8.   Held  thermometer  in  place  until  it  beeps,  then  removed  probe  from   ear.   
2  0  
  
9.   Read  the  temperature  on  the  screen.  
1  0  
  
10.   Removed  the  probe  cover  and  disposed  of  properly.  
2  0  
  
11.   Removed  gloves,  and  washed  hands  or  use  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
12.   Accurately  recorded  temperature  on  daily  record  sheet.  
4  0  
  
13.   Used appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient  and  other  personnel.  
2  0  
  
14.   Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill.

Home  Health  Aide  Skill  II:  Taking  an  Apical  Pulse  Time:  3  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________    Division:  ________ SS  ________ PS/C    Judge’s  Signature: _________________________
 
 Skill  II:  Taking  an  Apical  Pulse  Possible  Awarded  1.   
 Gathered  equipment:  stethoscope,  wristwatch  with  second  hand,  alcohol  wipes,  pen,  and    daily  record  sheet.  
1  0  
  
2.    Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
3.    Explained  skill  to  patient.  
2  0  
  
4.   Cleaned  stethoscope  diaphragm  and  earpieces.  
2  0  
  
5.   Correctly  placed  stethoscope  earpieces  in  ears.  
1  0  
  
6.   Placed  the  diaphragm  over  the  apex  of  the  patient’s  heart.  
1  0  
  
7.   Counted  the  louder  sound  (lub)  for  one  complete  minute.  
1  0  
  
8.   Removed  the  stethoscope  from  ears  and  patient.  
1  0  
  
9.   Washed  hands  or  use  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
10.   Accurately  recorded  apical  pulse  on  daily  record  sheet,  within  +  or  –  2  of  the  judges  count.  
4  0  
  
11.   Used appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient  and  other  personnel.  
2  0  
  
12.   Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill  
2  0

1  0    2.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene  and  put  on  gloves.  
2  0    3.   Explained  skill  to  patient.  
      2        0    4.   Placed  paper  towel  underneath  measuring  device  on  ﬂoor  below  drainage  bag.  
1  0    5.  a.  Opened  drain  or  spout  and  allowed  urine  to  drain  into  measuring  device.    
1  0    
b.  Avoided  allowing  tip  of  tubing  to  touch  sides  of  measuring  device.   
1  0    6.   Closed  drain,  wiped  it  with  the  alcohol  wipe,  and  replaced  it  in  the  holder  on  the  bag.  
1  0  
  
7.   Noted  amount  and  color  of  urine  (verbalized  to  judge).  
4  0    8.   Emptied  urine  into  toilet  (or  designated  container).  
1  0    9.   Washed  and  rinsed  measuring  device.  
1  0    10.   Removed  gloves  and  washed  hands  or  use  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.

Home  Health  Aide  Skill  IV:  Changing  a  Dry  Dressing  Using  Non-sterile  Technique
 
Time:  5  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________      Division:  ________ SS  ________ PS/C    Judge’s  Signature: ________________________
 
 Skill  IV:  Changing  a  Dry  Dressing  Using  Non-sterile  Technique  Possible  Awarded     1.   
Gathered  equipment:  gloves  (2  pair),  4X4  gauze  dressings,  waste  bag,  tape,  adhesive  remover  and  bandage  scissors,  disposable  bed  protector  or  paper  towel.  
1  0  
  
   2.    Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
3.    Explained  skill  to  patient.  
      2       0  
  
4.  
 Positioned  patient  so  area  with  dressing  is  accessible  while  maintaining  patient  comfort  and   privacy.  
1  0  
  
5.    Placed  supplies  on  a  clean  disposable  bed  protector  or  paper  towel  within  reach.    
1  0  
  
6.   Opened  gauze  package  without  touching  the  gauze.(maintaining  pad  sterility)  
2  0  
  
7.   Put  on  gloves 
1  0  
  
8.  a.  Removed  old  dressing.   
1  0  
  
b.  Noted  color,  amount  of  drainage,  and  condition  of  surrounding  skin  (verbalized  to  judge).  
4  0  
  
c.  Disposed  of  used  dressing  in  the  waste  bag.  
2  0  
  
d.  Remove  any  adhesive  from  skin  using  adhesive  remover. 
1  0  
  
e.  Removed  and  discarded  used  gloves.  
2  0  
  
f.  Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol  based  hand-rub  for  hand   hygiene.  
2  0  
  
9.   Put  on  new  gloves.  
2  0  
  
10.   Applied  dressing  without  touching  center,  holding  dressing  on  the  corners  only.  
2  0  
  
11.   Applied  tape  correctly.  
1  0  
  
12.   Positioned  patient  comfortably.  
1  0  
  
13.   Discarded  waste  and  returned  supplies  to  storage.  
2  0  
  
14.   Removed  gloves,  and  washed  hands  or  use  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
15.  
 Recorded  dressing  change  on  daily  record  sheet,  noting  observation  of  skin  condition,  that   dressing  was  changed,  and  any  patient  complaints.  
4  0  
  
16.   Used  appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient  and  other  personnel.  
2  0  
  
17.   Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill  
2  0

Home  Health  Aide  Skill  V:  Measuring  and  Recording  Intake  and  Output
 
Time:  5  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________      Division:  ________ SS  ________ PS/C     Judge’s  Signature: ________________________
 
 Skill  V:   Measuring  and  Recording  Intake  and  Output   Possible  Awarded  1.   Gathered  equipment:   I  &  O  sheet,  graduate  (measuring  container),  pen,  notepaper,  and  gloves.  
1  0  
 
 
2.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
 
 
3.   Explained  skill  to  patient.  
2  0  
 
 
4.   Provided  privacy  for  the  patient  (if  appropriate).  
1  0  
 
 
5.  
 INTAKE:    a.  Determined  amount  of  ﬂuid  intake  using  size  of  container  and  the  amount  consumed  
1  0  
 
 
b.  Noted  amount  on  notepaper.  
1  0  
 
 c.  If  measured  in  ounces,  converted  to  mL’s.    
2  0  
 
 6.   Washed  hand  or  used  alcohol–based  handrub.  
2  0  
 
 
7.   
 DOCUMENTING  INTAKE  a.  Documented  amount  of  ﬂuid  consumed  in  mL’s  on  I  &  O  form.  
2  0  
 
 
b.  Recorded  time  and  type  of  ﬂuid  consumed.  
2  0  
 
 c.  Reported  anything  unusual  that  was  observed,  such  as  patient  refusing  to  drink,  drinking  very  little,  or  feeling  nauseated.  
2  0  
 
 
8.  
 OUTPUT  a.  Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub.  
2  0  
 
 
b.  Put  on  gloves  before  handling  bedpan,  urinal,  or  foley  catheter  bag.  
2  0  
 
 c.  Emptied  contents  of  the  bedpan,urinal,  or  foley  catheter  bag  into  the  graduate  without  splashing.  If  the  bedpan  or  urinal  has  volume  markings,  note  the  amount.  
1  0  
 
 
d.  Placed  graduate  on  ﬂat  surface  and  measured  at  eye  level.  
1  0  
 
 e.  If  amount  is  between  measurement  lines,  round  up  to  the  nearest  25  mL.  
1  0  
 
 f.  Noted  the  amount  on  notepaper.  
1  0  
 
 9.  
 
 To  measure  vomitus:  a.  Poured  from  basin  into  measuring  container  and  added  to  output.  
1  0  
 
 
b.  If  vomit  is  on  ﬂoor  or  bed  -  estimated  amount  and  added  to  output.  
1  0  
 
 10.    Emptied  the  graduate  into  the  toilet  without  splashing.  
1  0  
 
 
11.    Rinsed  the  graduate  and  poured  rinse  water  into  the  toilet.  
1  0  
 
 
12.   
 Rinsed  the  bedpan/urinal  and  ﬂushed  in  toilet                Judge  will  award  points  if  a  catheter  bag  is  used.  
1  0  
 
 13.  
 Stored  the  bedpan/urinal  and  graduate                Judge  will  award  points  if  a  catheter  bag  is  used.  
1  0  
 
 14.   Removed  and  discarded  gloves.  
2  0  
 
 15.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub.  
2  0  
 
 16.   Documented  time  and  output  on  I  &  O  form.  
2  0

Home  Health  Aide  Skill  VI:  Caring  for  Dentures
 
Time:  5  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________      Division:  ________ SS  ________ PS/C     Judge’s  Signature: ________________________
 
 Skill  VI:   Caring  for  Dentures  Possible  Awarded  
1.   
 Gathered  equipment:  toothbrush,  toothpaste,  denture  cleaning  tablet,  denture  cup,  gloves,   mouthwash,  small  cup,  emesis  basin,  washcloth,  small  towel.  
1  0    
2.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene  and  put  on  gloves.  
2  0    
3.    Explained  skill  to  patient.  
    2      0    
4.    Asked  patient  to  remove  dentures  and  place  in  denture  cup.  
1  0    
5.   Placed  2-3  inches  cool  water  and  washcloth  in  bottom  of  sink.  
1  0    
6.   Removed  dentures  from  denture  cup  and  rinsed  dentures  placing  in  the  emesis  basin.  
1  0    
7.   Rinsed  denture  cup  and  ﬁlled  with  cold  water  and  denture  cleaning  tablet.  
1  0    
8.  
 Turned  on  cold  water  and  brushed  all  surfaces  of  the  upper  and  lower  plate  with  toothpaste   and  rinsed   
1  0    
9.   Placed  dentures  in  denture  cup.  
1  0    
10.   Rinsed  emesis  basin  and  toothbrush.  
1  0    
11.  
 Assisted  patient  to  rinse  mouth  with  mouthwash,  expel  rinse  in  emesis  basin  and  wipe    mouth.  
1  0    
12.  
 Described  (verbalized  to  the  judge)  the  use  of  toothettes  to  clean  the  gums  and  tongue  to    observe  the  condition  of  the  patient’s  mouth.  
2  0    
13.  
 Placed  the  denture  cup  within  reach  of  the  patient  and  instructed  patient  to  insert  dentures   when  needed.  
1  0    
14.  
 Removed  gloves,  washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene,  and    returned  supplies  to  their  proper  place.  
2  0    
15.  
 Recorded  completion  of  skill  on  daily  record  sheet,  noting  observation  of  skin  (oral  cavity)   condition  and  any  patient  complaints.  
4  0    
16.   Used  appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient  and  other  personnel.  
2  0    
17.   Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill.  
2  0

Home  Health  Aide   Skill  VII:  Moving  a  Patient  Up  in  Bed  Using  the  Drawsheet
 
Time:  3  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________      Division:  ________ SS  ________ PS/C    Judge’s  Signature: ________________________
 
 Skill  VII:   Moving  the  Patient  Up  in  Bed  Using  the  Drawsheet   Possible  Awarded  
1.   
 Ask  the  family  member  (judge  or  event  personnel)  to  help  you  move  the  patient  up  in  bed.    
1  0    
2.  
 Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0    
3.   
 Explained  skill  to  patient.  
2  0    
Instructed  the  family  member  (judge  or  event  personnel)  on  what  to  do  and  how  to  help  throughout  all  steps  of  the  skill,  as  needed.  (points  awarded  at  end  of  the  rating  sheet.)
 
 
4.  
 Placed  pillow  at  the  head  of  the  bed  to  protect  the  patient’s  head.  
2  0    
5.  
a.  Rolled  both  sides  of  the  drawsheet  (or  ﬂat  sheet  folded  in  fours)  toward  the  patient.  
1  0    
b.  Placed  the  patient’s  feet  12  inches  apart.  
1  0    
c.  Bent  the  patient’s  knees.  
1  0    
d.  With  the  hand  nearest  the  patient’s  feet,  grasped  the  rolled  drawsheet.  
1  0    e.  With  the  other  hand,  both  cradled  the  patient’s  head   and  shoulders  and  ﬁrmly  grasped  top  of  the  drawsheet.  
1  0    
6.  
 Turned  body  and  feet  toward  the  head  of  the  bed,  keeping  feet  12  inches  apart,  knees    slightly  bent.  
2  0    
7.  
 On  a  coordinated  count  of  3,  lifted  the  drawsheet  and  patient  up  toward  the  head  of  the  bed   without  dragging  the  patient.   
2  0    
8.  
 Aligned  patient’s  body  and  limbs,  placed  pillow  under  head,  tightened  drawsheet  and    replaced  covers.  
1  0    
9.  
 Communicated  appropriately  and  effectively  to  family  member  (judge  or  event  personnel)    throughout  skill.  
2  0    
10.  
 Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0    
11.  
 Recorded  completion  of  skill  and  patient  reaction  on  daily  record  sheet.  
4  0    
12.  
 Used  appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient  and  other  personnel.  
2  0    
13.  
 Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill.  
2  0    
                                                                                        TOTAL  POINTS  --  SKILL  VII                                                                                     70%  Mastery  for  Skill  VII  =20.3

Home  Health  Aide  Skill  VIII:  Applying  Elasticized  Stockings  (One  leg)
 
Time:  5  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________      Division:  ________ SS   ________ PS/C    Judge’s  Signature: ________________________
 
 Skill  VIII:  Applying  Elasticized  Stockings  (One  leg)  Possible  Awarded  
   1.    Gathered  equipment:   knee-length  elasticized  /  compression  stockings.  
1  0  
  
2.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
3.    Explained  skill  to  patient.  
2      0  
  
4.   With  patient  lying  in  bed  supine,  exposed  the  leg  indicated  in  the  scenario.  
4      0  
  
5.   Turned  stocking  inside  out  to  heel  by  placing  hand  inside  stocking  and  grasping  heel.  
1  0  
  
6.  
a.  Positioned  stocking  over  the  foot  and  heel  of  patient  making  sure  the  heel  of  the  stocking  is  in  the  proper  place.  
1  0  
  
 b.  Slid  the  remaining  stocking  over  the  foot  and  heel.  
1  0  
  
c.  Continued  to  pull  the  stocking  over  the  calf  to  the  knee.  
1  0  
  
7.   Checked  to  be  sure  stocking  is  applied  evenly  and  smoothly  with  no  wrinkles.  
2  0  
  
8.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
9.   Recorded  completion  of  skill  and  patient  reaction  on  daily  record  sheet.  
4  0  
  
10.    Used  appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient  and  other  personnel.  
2  0  
  
11.   Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill.  
2  0
